lead_with.title: Answer his exact question
lead_with.text: He asked how the AI "stands out and adds value to the patient's experience" and for a **publication**. Lead with the patient story: rare-disease patients wait years for a diagnosis, and DNA-only tests solve **under 40%** of cases (PhiTech's 2026 funding coverage). G&M reads **DNA and RNA together** to shorten that wait. Attach the founders' peer-reviewed work, and say plainly what is and is not yet validated.

lead_with.title: Close to home, not in-house
lead_with.text: GVMH does not sequence; it sends tests out. Pitch G&M as decision support that helps **GVMH's oncologists and maternal-fetal medicine team** get a clearer answer from sequencing ordered through reference labs — so patients stay in Clinton instead of being referred to Kansas City.

lead_with.title: Ask for the door, not the deal
lead_with.text: Shawn is a 20-year lab leader and a former **market director for a multi-hospital lab service line** (CHI Health Midwest). Ask him which reference lab or pathology group (Quest, MAWD Pathology) and which network (the new **Show-Me High Value Network** of 24 independent Missouri hospitals) would be the right home for this.

person.name: Shawn Walters
person.text: Laboratory Director at Golden Valley Memorial Healthcare since September 2022, overseeing the lab's operations and compliance with policies and standards. Previously **Market Director, Laboratory Service Line, CHI Health, Midwest Region** (Omaha, NE). More than 20 years of laboratory experience. BS in Chemistry (University of Nebraska Omaha), BS in Biological Science (Peru State College), Cytotechnology certificate (University of Nebraska Medical Center), and **ASCP certification in Laboratory Management**.

company.text: Golden Valley Memorial Healthcare (Clinton, MO) has served west-central Missouri for more than 50 years. It is a 56-bed hospital — the only one for three rural counties across an 80-mile radius — with a 24/7 emergency department, four multispecialty clinics, a cancer center (medical and radiation oncology, chemotherapy, infusion, mobile mammography), a birthing center and maternal-fetal medicine, ambulance service and a 340B-funded diabetes program. CEO is **Craig Thompson**. CMS rated it 5 stars (per AHA, 2023) and Becker's named it a Great Community Hospital in 2025. Recent moves: **da Vinci 5** robotic surgery (Jan 2026), a **~US$4M HRSA rural maternal-health grant** as hub of a six-county program (Sep 2026), joining the **Show-Me High Value Network** with 23 other independent Missouri hospitals (Sep 2026), a family medicine residency build-out, and a **specialty pharmacy** opened Oct 19, 2026.

financials.text: **FY ended Mar 31, 2023 (audited, Missouri State Auditor filing):** total operating revenue **US$154.3M**; net patient service revenue US$139.8M; operating income **US$8.8M**; net position US$132.3M; cash US$14.6M. **Federal awards spent:** US$9.66M in the 2024 audit year (Federal Audit Clearinghouse; auditor Forvis Mazars), mainly Provider Relief, disaster and USDA rural programs. **Payer mix (2023):** ~60% Medicare, ~20% Medicaid, ~20% commercial — margins depend on 340B savings. The separate **GVMH Foundation** (501(c)(3)) had US$0.79M revenue and US$3.8M net assets (FY Mar 2025). Read: profitable for a rural hospital but grant- and Medicare-dependent; new spend is easier when tied to a grant or measurable savings.

industry.title: Rural money is moving
industry.text: Missouri won **US$216.3M** in year one of the federal Rural Health Transformation Program (Dec 2025). Its plan funds a statewide **data "digital backbone"**, regional networks and service grants for **obstetrics and oncology** — two GVMH lines.

industry.title: Independent hospitals team up
industry.text: GVMH joined 23 other independent Missouri hospitals in the **Show-Me High Value Network** (Sep 2026) for quality, care coordination and value-based care. Shared services across members are the realistic route for niche tools.

industry.title: Beyond DNA-only testing
industry.text: Rare disease affects ~400 million people worldwide and diagnosis often takes years; PhiTech's case is that adding RNA to DNA analysis lifts the share of cases solved. For a rural hospital this means fewer referrals out and shorter diagnostic odysseys.

talking_points: When a GVMH oncologist or your maternal-fetal medicine team needs a genetic answer today, where does the test go and who interprets it?
How often do rare or unexplained cases get referred to larger centers for a diagnosis — and what does that cost patients in time and travel?
What evidence would you need to see before recommending an AI decision-support tool to your medical staff — peer-reviewed papers, US validation, a reference-lab partner?
Would MAWD Pathology or Quest be the right partner to run G&M on sequencing data for GVMH patients?
Is genomics part of what the Show-Me High Value Network or Missouri's rural transformation plan might fund for oncology or obstetrics?
Who besides you would sit in on a demo — pathology, oncology, MFM, IT?
